newsitem.title: USA: U.S. West Coast gasolines flat, refiners back out.
newsitem.headline: U.S. West Coast gasolines flat, refiners back out.

text.p: U.S. West Coast gasoline prices flattened Wednesday, as refiners backed out of the marketafter yesterday's late buying frenzy, brokers said.
Afternoon trade turned quiet, with no deals heard done.
Los Angeles CARB unleaded gasoline prices, which rose 2.50 to three cents Tuesday, were unchanged at 75.50/76 cents Wednesday.

Last night's inventory data from the American Petroleum Institute (API) spooked California traders into buying after it reported West Coast gasoline stocks fell 1.3 million, adding to three week decline of two million barrels.
Conventional gasoline in Los Angeles was talked 71/72 cents a gallon, equal to Tuesday levels. Premium stood seven cents higher.
Distillates in San Francisco and L.A. were narrowly mixed in quiet trade.
